verses.1: In the thirty-first year of his reign, Josiah ruled. He ruled in Jerusalem for thirty-one years.
verses.2: And he did what was right in the eyes of Jehovah. He followed the ways of his father David. He did not turn to the right or left.
verses.3: And in his reign, he spent two years. He still was a young man when he began to worship the God of his father, David. After twenty-two years, he began to purify Judah and Jerusalem from all those who were unclean, corrupt, and evil people.
verses.4: And they set up before him the idols of the gods and heroes who lived long ago. They also set up the idols of the sun, moon, stars, and other celestial beings. They placed these idols on the faces of the graves.
verses.5: And those high places were destroyed on their altars. Thus, Judah and Jerusalem were purified.
verses.6: And in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, Shemuel, and Ad-Naphtali, during their destructions.
verses.7: And he destroyed the altars, as well as all the idols and sacred objects. He also destroyed all the golden vessels that were in use throughout the land of Israel. Then he returned to Jerusalem.
verses.8: And in the twelfth year of his reign, he sent Shaphan son of Azariah, along with the officials who governed the city, and Yoahaz son of Yoahaziah, to strengthen the house of Jehovah, God.
verses.9: And they went to Chilqiyah, where the high priest was. They gave him the money that had been brought to the house of God. This money had been collected by Menashe and Efrayim, along with all the other Israelites and Jews. Then they returned to Jerusalem.
verses.10: And they were given to those who were responsible for doing the work in the house of Jehovah. They were given to those workers who worked in the house of Jehovah, in order to strengthen and reinforce the building itself.
verses.11: And they gave to their descendants and children the ability to buy stone and wood for building purposes, so that they could repair the temples that had been destroyed by the kings of Judah.
verses.12: And the men work in sincerity during their labor. They are supervised by those who are responsible for them. The people from the tribes of Merari and Zevulun, as well as those from the tribes of Kohathim, serve God. All those who understand the laws of music also serve God.
verses.13: And upon those who are slaves and those who die in labor, for all those who do work and labor. And also upon those who are scribes, porters, and gatekeepers.
verses.14: And when they brought out the money that had been brought to the house of Jehovah, the priest found in Moses’ hand the book of the Torah of Jehovah.
verses.15: And Hilkiah said to Shaphan, the scribe: “I found the Book of the Law in the house of the LORD.” Then Hilkiah handed the book over to Shaphan.
verses.16: And Shaphan brought the scroll to the king. He then sat down again before the king and said, “All that has been given to your servants has indeed been done.”
verses.17: They took the money that was found in the Temple of Jehovah, and they handed it over to the administrators and to those who were responsible for managing the Temple’s affairs.
verses.18: And the scribe reported to the king, “The priest gave me some of his share.” Then the scribe stood before the king and said these words.
verses.19: And when the king heard the words of the prophet, he tore his clothes in anger.
verses.20: And the king commanded that Chalilah and Ahikam be given to Shephen, and that Abdon and Michah be given to him. Also, Shaphan, the scribe, and Asiya, the servant of the king, were given to him as well.
verses.21: Go and seek Jehovah for me, and for those who remain in Israel and in Judah. Seek to fulfill the words written in the Book, which are truly great and wonderful. These words were given to us by Jehovah, so that we might carry out all that is written in this Book.
verses.22: And Chiliyahu went there. And the king sent El-Huldah, the prophet’s wife, who was the daughter of Takhat and the daughter of Hasra. She lived in Jerusalem during that time. They spoke to her about certain things.
verses.23: And He said to them, “As the LORD God of Israel says: ‘Tell the man who sent you to me that he may go away from here.’”
verses.24: So said Jehovah: “I will bring calamity upon this place and its inhabitants. All those curses written in the book that was read before the king of Judah shall be carried out against them.”
verses.25: Under the circumstances in which they abandoned me and chose other gods instead, so that they could provoke me with all their actions. My anger will still be there, in this place, and it will never fade away.
verses.26: And to the king of Judah, who has sent you to be taught by Jehovah, say to him these words: “Thus says Jehovah, the God of Israel: These are the words that you have heard.”
verses.27: Because your heart is merciful, you will obey God’s commands. You will listen to His words regarding this place and its inhabitants. You will bow down before Him, tear your clothes apart, and lay them before Him. And I have also heard these words from Jehovah.
verses.28: I will bring you back to your ancestors, and you will be brought back to your graves in peace. Your eyes will not see all the evil that I will bring upon this place and its inhabitants. And the king will be restored to his throne.
verses.29: And the king sent for all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.30: And the king went into the Temple of God, along with all the Jews and the people of Jerusalem, as well as the priests, the Levites, and all the people, from the greatest to the smallest. They heard all the words of the covenant that were written in the Temple of God.
verses.31: And the king stood firm in his position, and he made a covenant before Jehovah. He vowed to follow Jehovah’s commands, laws, and regulations with all his heart and soul, so that he could carry out the words of the covenant written on that scroll.
verses.32: And he stood against all those who were found in Jerusalem and in Nain. And the people of Jerusalem did what was right in the eyes of God, the God of their ancestors.
verses.33: And Josiah removed all the idols from all the lands belonging to the Israelites. He made sure that everyone in Israel would serve only Jehovah, their God. All his days were spent serving Jehovah, their God. He never stopped serving Jehovah, the God of his ancestors.
